requirements.text: For CS-0001127 ... first confirm that the account is still covered under an Enterprise-level support entitlement ... Once eligibility is verified, shift the case into in progress
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 1127 AND state = 'in_progress'
assumptions: CS-0001127 is case_id 1127 (account 49 Hernandez, Barnett and Stewart; product 165 Fortinet FortiGate 100F Variant 33, the network security product; pending; critical)

eligibility holds on the seed: entitlement 399 is enterprise, account-wide (product_id NULL), active, on contract 121 (active, 2025-09-24 to 2026-11-14), so the gated change is required; the product-specific entitlement 400 is only standard, and the second account-wide enterprise entitlement 402 sits on contract 122, which ended 2026-10-15
pending -> in_progress is a valid transition under the policy's lifecycle

requirements.text: shift the case into in progress so the assigned team can continue with diagnostics and remediation
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_sla WHERE case_id = 1127 AND sla_def_id = 1 AND stage = 'in_progress'
assumptions: policy: when a case moves to work in progress the appropriate SLA is aligned to it; sla_def 1 (SLA Response - Critical, active, applies_to_priority critical) is the response definition for the case's critical priority
two case_sla rows are created, so each is selected by its natural key (case and definition), not by id (the ids would be 2466 and 2467)
the seed already holds a paused row (2253) for this definition; the count is 1 whether the agent links a new in_progress row (tool link_new_case_sla) or resumes the paused one, and 2 if it does both

requirements.text: shift the case into in progress so the assigned team can continue with diagnostics and remediation
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_sla WHERE case_id = 1127 AND sla_def_id = 6 AND stage = 'in_progress'
assumptions: sla_def 6 (SLA Resolution - Critical, active, applies_to_priority critical) is the resolution definition for the case's critical priority
selected by natural key, not by id, as above; the seed's paused row for this definition is 2254

requirements.text: Update the priority to high, move the case to resolved, and allow it to proceed toward closure
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 888 AND priority = 'high' AND state = 'resolved'
assumptions: CS-0000888 is case_id 888 (account 38 Stark, Petersen and Palmer; product 156 APC Smart-UPS SRT3000 Variant 24, the power product; in_progress; low); in_progress -> resolved is valid
'allow it to proceed toward closure' means the case stops at resolved (the policy forbids closing directly), so the state cell also fails if the case is closed

'noting that the adjustment reflects elevated business impact' is read as the stated reason for the priority change, not as an escalation; the schema has no case note table and the request does not ask to escalate

requirements.text: shift the case into in progress so the assigned team can continue
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_sla WHERE case_id = 1127 AND sla_def_id NOT IN (1, 6)
assumptions: boundary of 'appropriate SLA': definitions for other priorities and the inactive global ones (5, 10) must not be linked to a critical case
disagreement: this stay is A only (B had no such requirement); kept because it is the boundary of the SLA-definition selector: 'appropriate SLA' admits only the critical definitions

notes: Merged from two passes that agree on the four shared requirements (anchors, natural-key selectors, values) and on all four dispositions (kept). disagreement: A's stay that no SLA definition outside 1 and 6 is linked to case 1127 (B had no such requirement); kept because it is the boundary of the SLA-definition selector (logged in the requirement). disagreement: A's stay that case 1120 (account 49's other open case on product 165) keeps state new (B had no such requirement); dropped because the request names the case by its number, CS-0001127 is unique on the seed, so no loose reading of the lookup reaches 1120 and the stay is a generic invariant. disagreement: A's stay that case 886 (account 38's other open case on the same UPS product) keeps priority moderate and state new (B had no such requirement); dropped for the same reason, CS-0000888 being unique. The entitlement check is a read, not a write: it holds on the seed (entitlement 399, enterprise, account-wide, active, contract 121 valid to 2026-11-14), so the state change on 1127 is due. Case 1127 already carries paused case_sla rows for definitions 1 and 6 (2253, 2254); the benchmark's checks, the tool list (link_new_case_sla, no SLA update tool) and the policy's 'aligned to it' point to new in_progress rows, and the natural-key selectors accept a resume of the paused rows equally. The priority change on case 888 would imply high-priority SLA targets, but the request does not ask to re-align its SLAs (paused rows for the low definitions 4 and 9) and the policy ties alignment to the move into in progress, so none is required. 'Noting that the adjustment reflects elevated business impact' is not turned into escalation = 1 / escalation_reason = 'impact'. Acting user Jose Roberson (user 32) is an admin whose row is inactive on the seed (active = 0); the policy's default admin role is applied, as the benchmark's checks assume. Least sure: dropping the two case stays, since the request also describes each case by account and product, which a search_cases lookup by description could match twice. revised: the reasons for keeping the SLA-definition stay and for dropping the case stays are stated directly, not by reference to other files or to a rule.
